en.html:
Hikaru"Ow."
Kageaki"Listen properly."
Hikaru"It is not that I am unwilling to make an effort to try."
Kageaki"One day you will succeed Lady Subaru as the Minato priestess. Unless you master at least the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki, you will be embarrassed later."
Hikaru"Bored..."
Kageaki"Until you have studied enough to be bored, it does not become knowledge."
Hikaru"Only Yamato myths, all the time."
Kageaki"Naturally."
Hikaru"Sometimes I want a different story."
Kageaki"For language and arithmetic, better to learn properly from your schoolteachers than from me."
Hikaru"I dislike their talking. They just go on by themselves. Whether we are listening or not, no concern."
Hikaru"Your voice feels nice after I listen, so I sleep. Their voices I dislike, so I sleep before listening."
Kageaki"...Is that why your marks are poor?"

Kageaki"...Also, my lessons are not lullabies."
Hikaru"Ow..."
Kageaki"We continue."
Hikaru"Different storyyy."
Kageaki"..."
Kageaki"What sort of story do you want?"
Hikaru"Hmm."
Hikaru"A story about different gods?"
Kageaki"Outside Yamato?"
Hikaru"Yes."
Kageaki"Myths are not so different from country to country. Only the gods' names change."
Kageaki"...No, perhaps that is saying too much..."
Hikaru"For example?"
Kageaki"In Greek myth... first there was ChaosChaos. From it came EarthGaia, the UnderworldTartarus, LoveEros, then DarknessErebus and NightNyx. From Darkness and Night came LightAether and DayHemera."
Kageaki"EarthGaia gave birth to SkyUranus and SeaPontus."
Hikaru"Ooh..."
Kageaki"See? Much the same."
Hikaru"Entirely different."
Kageaki"...Hm? Well, it depends on interpretation..."
Hikaru"Continue."
Kageaki"...SkyUranus ruled the world. With EarthGaia as his wife, he fathered the Hundred-Handed GiantsHecatoncheires and the One-Eyed GiantsCyclopes. But Sky disliked these giants and cast them into the UnderworldTartarus."
Hikaru"Cruel."

en.html:
Kageaki"Afterwards, SkyUranus and EarthGaia had twelve Great GodsTitans... But Earth resented Sky's treatment of the giants, and ordered the Great Gods to overthrow their father."
Kageaki"The youngest of the twelve, AgricultureCronus, accomplished it. Yet he committed the same offense as his father, and was overthrown by his own son in turn."
Kageaki"That son was the Chief GodZeus. With him as king, the gods entered their golden age."
Hikaru"Interesting."
Kageaki"Is it?"
Hikaru"More!"
Kageaki"No. Enough. Back to the Kojiki."
Hikaru"Moreee."
Kageaki"...Another time."
Hikaru"Hmph."
Kageaki"Pouting will not change it."
Hikaru"Then a question."
Kageaki"What?"
Hikaru"Uranus・・・・ and Gaia・・・ became the rulers of their family together, yes?"
Kageaki"Yes."
Hikaru"But Gaia brought Uranus into the world?"
Kageaki"...That is right."
Hikaru"Then he claimed authority over the very person who made him?"
Kageaki"That is what the story says."
Hikaru"Is that not forbidden?"
Kageaki"For humans."
Hikaru"Not for gods, then?"
Kageaki"...Gods probably have rules of their own."
Hikaru"Hmm."
Kageaki"Now, back to the lesson."
Hikaru"Yeees..."

en.html:
Her father had broken human rules, and <ruby>therefore<rt>therefore</rt></ruby> could not be her father. Had abandoned being her father.

That was not necessarily what he himself wanted. But this world's law had not permitted him to be her father.

In the end, he had obeyed that law. So he would never appear before Hikaru as her father.

One could say social order had taken him away from her. If Hikaru became a destroyer of the world because she wanted him back—perhaps that was not madness after all. Perhaps it had its own logic.

That was not necessarily what he himself wanted. But this world's law had not permitted him to be her father.

In the end, he had obeyed that law. So he would never appear before Hikaru as her father.

One could say social order had taken him away from her. If Hikaru became a destroyer of the world because she wanted him back—perhaps that was not madness after all. Perhaps it had its own logic.

ja.html:
父は人の道に背き、
　<ruby>故<rt>ゆえ</rt></ruby>に父たり得ず、父たる事を捨てた。

　それは必ずしも父の本意ではなかった。
　しかしこの世の法が、父の父たる事を認めなかった。

　結局、父は法に従った。
　だから決して、父として光の前に現れる事はない。

　言うなれば光の父は、社会秩序に奪われた。
　光が父を欲して世界の破壊者たるのなら――確かに
それは狂気ではなく、道理なのかもしれない。

en.html:
I thought of the anguish of the man who was my adoptive father.

Since then, what feelings had he carried through his life? Regret... resignation?

And now, if he learned Hikaru's wish, what would he think? That to recover her father, she had become “Silver Star,” removed her mother, sought to destroy the world and surpass humanity to become a god—reached the utmost extreme of violence.

What would he think?

ja.html:
俺にとって養父である人の苦悩を思う。

　あの人はあれから、どんな想いを胸に宿して生きて
きたのだろう。
　後悔か……諦観か。

　そして今、光の望みを知ったなら、何を思うだろう。
　父を取り戻すという望みのために〝銀星号〟となり、
母を排除し世界を壊し、人を越えて、神たらんとする
――暴挙の極致へ至ったのだと知ったなら。

　何を思うか。

en.html:
What should I think?

Back then, I had not reached an age to understand responsibility. But that was no defense. In the end, the decision which erased Hikaru's father—and led to today—had been mine.

What should I think?
What should I do?

ja.html:
俺こそ、何を思うべきか。

　あの頃、俺は責任の意味を理解できる年齢に達して
いなかった。
　だがそれは弁明にならない。最終的に光の父を抹消
し――今日の事態を導いたのは、俺の決断であるから。

　何を思うべきか。
　何をするべきか。
